skill.name: brenda-database
skill.description: Access BRENDA enzyme database data through the SOAP API for kinetic parameters, reaction equations, organism data, and substrate-specific enzyme analysis.
skill.summary: Query BRENDA enzyme data for kinetics, reactions, organisms, and pathway analysis.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, EC enzyme numbers, standard imports, credential setup docs, and local export helpers. One semantic concern remains: evaluation_output.json embeds audit-style safety claims that could bias automated review. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, shell execution, C2 behavior, or obfuscated code in the cited scripts.

remediation.issue: Bundled self-audit file asserts marketplace safety.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_output.json from the published skill package or move it outside source artifacts.
Keep examples placeholder-only and document secret handling for BRENDA_EMAIL and BRENDA_PASSWORD.

remediation.issue: Export helpers write to caller-provided file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Default exports to a dedicated output directory and document overwrite behavior for user-supplied filenames.

content.value_statement: Enzyme research often needs reliable kinetic and reaction data from literature. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code query BRENDA and summarize enzyme evidence.
actual_capabilities: Query BRENDA SOAP methods for Km values, reactions, organism filters, and substrate filters.
Parse BRENDA response fields into organism, substrate, kinetic value, commentary, and literature data.
Search enzymes by substrate, product, reaction pattern, organism, and environmental condition.
Compare enzyme properties across organisms for metabolic engineering and enzyme selection.
Export query results and pathway reports to CSV, JSON, Excel, text, or visualization files.
limitations: Requires a valid BRENDA account and API credentials.
Depends on optional Python packages such as zeep, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, and networkx.
Results depend on BRENDA coverage and may omit enzymes with sparse literature data.
SOAP queries can be slow or rate limited during broad wildcard searches.

use_cases.title: Compare enzyme kinetics
use_cases.description: Retrieve Km and kcat data for one enzyme across organisms, substrates, and reported experimental conditions.

use_cases.title: Select pathway enzymes
use_cases.description: Identify enzymes that support a target reaction and compare available organisms, cofactors, and feasibility notes.

use_cases.title: Find stable variants
use_cases.description: Search for thermophilic or pH-stable homologs before planning mutation, screening, or process work.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One Enzyme
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Km values and reaction data for EC 1.1.1.1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Summarize substrates, units, and citations.

prompt_templates.title: Filter by Substrate
prompt_templates.prompt: Find enzymes that act on glucose. Show EC numbers, organisms, reaction summaries, and reported kinetic values when available.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Organisms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare alcohol dehydrogenase data for Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and Homo sapiens. Highlight conditions and data gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Pathway Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-step enzymatic route to lactate from pyruvate. Include enzyme alternatives, organisms, conditions, and feasibility warnings.

output_examples.input: Find Km values for alcohol dehydrogenase in yeast.
output: Alcohol dehydrogenase results list ethanol and NAD+ substrates for Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
The summary includes reported Km values, experimental pH, temperature, and literature references.
Entries with missing conditions are marked as incomplete evidence.

output_examples.input: Compare glucose enzymes across common laboratory organisms.
output: The comparison ranks candidate enzymes by organism coverage and available kinetic data.
It separates direct glucose substrates from related phosphorylated compounds.
The result notes where BRENDA has sparse or inconsistent records.

output_examples.input: Find an enzymatic route to lactate from pyruvate.
output: The pathway review identifies candidate reaction steps and enzyme classes.
It lists likely organisms, cofactors, and environmental conditions.
Feasibility notes flag missing kinetics and broad database matches.

best_practices: Use exact EC numbers and organism names before trying wildcard searches.
Cache repeated BRENDA results and respect rate limits during batch work.
Validate parsed kinetic values against original BRENDA entries before modeling.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad wildcards without limits on large enzyme families.
Do not treat missing BRENDA data as evidence that an enzyme does not exist.
Do not store real BRENDA passwords in shared prompts, reports, or repositories.

faq.question: What is BRENDA?
faq.answer: BRENDA is a curated enzyme database with kinetic, reaction, organism, ligand, and literature information.

faq.question: Do I need credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. BRENDA SOAP access requires a registered account and API credentials.

faq.question: What are EC numbers?
faq.answer: EC numbers classify enzyme activities by reaction type, such as 1.1.1.1 for alcohol dehydrogenase.

faq.question: Can it compare organisms?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper scripts compare enzyme data across organisms when BRENDA has matching records.

faq.question: Can it export results?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts include export helpers for local CSV, JSON, Excel, text, and plot outputs.

faq.question: Are results always complete?
faq.answer: No. BRENDA coverage depends on published literature, so some enzymes or organisms have limited data.
